feeds.title: Ancient Origins
feeds.description: The goal of Ancient Origins is to highlight recent archaeological discoveries, peer-reviewed academic research and evidence, as well as offering alternative viewpoints and explanations of science, archaeology, mythology, religion and history around the globe.

feeds.title: The Ancient World Online
feeds.description: The primary focus of AWOL is to notice and comment on open access material relating to the ancient world. AWOL is a project of Charles E. Jones, Tombros Librarian for Classics and Humanities at the Pattee Library, Penn State University

feeds.title: Karwansaray Publishers » Ancient History
feeds.description: Ancient History looks at every aspect of the ancient world: you'll find articles covering politics, society, literature, language, religion, economics, and art - all in one magazine!

feeds.title: Ancient Pages
feeds.description: Founded in 2009, Ancient Pages is today one of the world's largest sites covering all about the ancient world. If you are interested in ancient mysteries, history, myths, legends, sacred writings, Biblical mysteries, and archaeology news - then you have come to the right place.

feeds.title: All Thats Interesting » Ancient History
feeds.description: From Greece to South America, All That's Interesting shares fascinating facts and interesting articles about ancient history! All That's Interesting is a place for seekers. From the lesser-known byways of human history to the uncharted corners of today's world, All That's Interesting seeks out the stories that illuminate our past, present, and future.

feeds.title: World History Encyclopedia
feeds.description: We are a non-profit organization publishing the world's most-read history encyclopedia. Our mission is to engage people with cultural heritage and to improve history education worldwide.

feeds.title: History Hit » Ancient
feeds.description: History Hit brings you the stories that shaped the world through our award-winning podcast network and an online history channel. We are passionate about the past and aim to bring it to new audiences across modern channels and new mediums.

feeds.title: Nobulart
feeds.description: Exploring the Great Reset. A web of interlinked original and historical articles that reveal the threads that connect our current experience with ancient secret societies, agendas, and beliefs.

feeds.title: Mini Museum Blog
feeds.description: The Mini Museum Shop offers a wide range of science and history collections featuring rare specimens. Customers can explore categories like Fossils & Geology, Air & Space, Jewelry, Relics & Artifacts, Faces & Places, and more. The shop showcases unique items such as meteorites, dinosaur fossils, jewelry inspired by history, and authentic artifacts. Customers can also find complete collections, gift options, and educational resources in their online store.

feeds.title: ISAW News
feeds.description: ISAW is a center for advanced scholarly research and graduate education, which aims to encourage particularly the study of the economic, religious, political, and cultural connections between ancient civilizations.

feeds.title: ScienceDaily News » Ancient Civilization
feeds.description: Archaeology news. Articles on ancient Egypt, ancient Rome, ancient Greece, and other civilizations. ScienceDaily is your source for the latest research news.

feeds.title: A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry Blog
feeds.description: Take a look at history and popular culture in A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry blog by Dr. Bret C. Devereaux, an ancient historian specializing in the Roman economy and military.

feeds.title: The History Blog » Ancient
feeds.description: My interests are primarily European ancient and medieval, but I'm quite undiscriminating when it comes to history, so I'll pretty much blather about anything that catches my eye.

feeds.title: Sententiae Antiquae
feeds.description: Are you in search of the 'wisdom' of the ancients, but don't know where to begin? Are you looking for more than the locus classicus--do you long for the odd and the obscure as well? Then you've come to the right place! Through this blog, we aim to bring you some of the most famous (and also most confounding) quotations from the ancient world.

feeds.title: Roger Pearse Blog
feeds.description: Thoughts on Antiquity, Patristics, putting things online, information access, and more. Welcome to my blog, I'm interested in the ancient world, and the early Christians within it; in the ancient texts and the manuscripts in which these reach us; and in the free circulation of information about all this online.

feeds.title: PaleoJudaica.com
feeds.description: Find the latest news on ancient Judaism and the biblical world.

feeds.title: Found in Antiquity Blog
feeds.description: Classical worlds, medieval culture and ancient Christianity. I'm Carla Hurt, a Latin high school teacher and youtuber who has converted to input-based approaches. My goal is to make engaging, learner-friendly content in Latin and Ancient Greek. I want the beauty and richness of ancient languages to be more accessible to people of all backgrounds, learning abilities, ages, and interests.

feeds.title: Biblonia
feeds.description: Handwritten, printed, digital - a blog about ancient, medieval and late-modern book cultures.

feeds.title: Sphinx Blog
feeds.description: I'm Neville Morley, Professor of Classics & Ancient History at the University of Exeter UK and author of such significant works on classical antiquity as 'Civil war and succession crisis in Roman beekeeping' and 'Thucydides, history, and historicism in Wilhelm Roscher'.

feeds.title: Roman Times
feeds.description: An online magazine about current archaeology and classical research into the lives of inhabitants of the Roman Empire and Byzantium and the civilizations around them.

feeds.title: Ingenia History
feeds.description: Ingenia explores the innovations and breakthroughs of the ancient world. From breathtakingly ornate masterpieces of Egyptian jewelry to hypothesized theories of medicine by the Greeks, all exemplify the revolutionary thinking and work of our past. This blog is a journey to ancient civilizations.

feeds.title: The Edithorial
feeds.description: Articles on ancient history by Edith Hall.

feeds.title: Roman History
feeds.description: Blogging Roman History for your edification.

feeds.title: Kiwi Hellenist
feeds.description: Modern myths about the ancient world. Peter Gainsford is a classicist based in Wellington, New Zealand. He is the author of Early Greek Hexameter Poetry (Cambridge, 2015) and has written articles on many aspects of Greek language, literature, and myth.

feeds.title: Mike Anderson's Ancient History Blog
feeds.description: History of ancient Rome and Greece including political systems and culture by Mike Anderson.

feeds.title: Examining The Bible
feeds.description: Examining The Bible is a non-sectarian educational website dedicated to promoting the academic study of the Bible, and making biblical studies and the wider history of ancient Israel widely accessible and available to everyone to read for leisure. The site was started by Josiah Selednik in 2023. Here, you will find articles, videos, and other educational content surrounding biblical history and biblical study.

feeds.title: Ancient Heroes Blog
feeds.description: Get the latest episode updates and exciting historical facts in the blog. Ancient Heroes is a podcast by history buff Patrick Garvey focused on exploring the history and mythology of the ancient world. Archaeologists and scholars join to discuss ancient Greece, Rome, Egypt, and other civilizations of the distant past.

feeds.title: Historical Easter Eggs Today in History Blog » Ancient History
feeds.description: Posts about Ancient History written by Cape Cod Curmudgeon. In this country, we're all free citizens of a self-governing Republic. We can't know where we want our country to go if we don't understand where it's been. It's one of the principal benefits of examining history.

feeds.title: Sarah E. Bond
feeds.description: Musings on daily life in the ancient and early medieval Mediterranean by Sarah E. Bond.

feeds.title: Faces&Voices
feeds.description: Articles on people, artefacts, and ancient history. Faces&Voices is the blog of Roberta Mazza, lecturer in Classics and Ancient History at the University of Manchester.

feeds.title: Penelope's Weavings and Unpickings
feeds.description: My name is Penelope Goodman. I'm a Senior Lecturer in Roman history, a Gothic horror and Doctor Who fan, and a Lib Dem. This blog is my place for weaving and unpicking the threads of anything which interests me.

feeds.title: AncientBlogger
feeds.description: Hi there, I'm an ancient blogger and this is my site with different ancient history content for all levels of interest. Vlogs, podcasts, and articles. It's all here!
